page: OVHcloud b3-256-flex is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor platform running under KVM virtualization. The configuration allocates 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, clocked at a baseline of 2.3 GHz. Memory capacity totals 256 GB of RAM, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. Local storage is limited to a bundled 50 GB NVMe SSD, and networking capabilities feature a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without included complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate exceptional parallel compute and in-memory throughput. Multi-core performance under stress-ng places the instance in the top 10% with a score of 194,581.4, complemented by top-tier multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 770.26 GB/sec. Redis SET operations reach 126.71 million operations per second, supported by high cached memory bandwidth of 8,300.17 GB/sec and 205.98 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth. Conversely, memory write throughput and single-threaded compression land in the middle tier, with single-core stress-ng rating in the top 25%.

Given its 64 dedicated non-hyperthreaded cores and high memory density, the instance offers strong qualitative compute efficiency for scaled workloads without hardware accelerator requirements. Primary hardware tradeoffs include modest bundled local storage of 50 GB NVMe and absence of default public IPv4 addressing, requiring external network configuration and supplementary storage volumes for heavy persistence. The platform is well matched for distributed in-memory caching, multi-threaded data processing, static web serving throughput, and large container orchestration.
description: OVHcloud b3-256-flex is a general-purpose virtual server configured with 64 dedicated AMD EPYC physical cores clocked at 2.3 GHz and 256 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Built on x86_64 architecture and managed via KVM, the instance integrates a 50 GB NVMe SSD for root operations alongside a 16 Gbps baseline network interface, while excluding GPUs and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark profiles indicate top-tier parallel compute capability, demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core metric of 194,581.4 and Redis SET performance reaching 126.71 million operations per second. However, storage capacity is strictly minimal, making the instance dependent on external storage attachments for high-capacity persistence. The configuration is primarily suited for CPU-intensive parallel processing, in-memory key-value databases, static web serving, and containerized enterprise services.
